purpose: Compare a verified prior workflow with the product-enabled workflow without inventing performance claims.
whenToUse: Both workflows can be represented from verified facts
The contrast makes the product value easier to understand
whenNotToUse: The before state would be a straw man
The comparison depends on unsourced time, cost, or quality numbers

layoutContract.comparison: Use matched scale, framing, and visual weight for both states.

motionContract.entrance: Establish the before state, then reveal the after state with one continuous axis.
motionContract.determinism: Use fixed states and a finite transition.
motionContract.continuity: Hold the final comparison long enough to read both labels.

transitionOptions.use: Reveal the after state across a matched split.
Use for full-frame states that cannot share a split.

captionRules.copy: Describe the verified difference without numerical improvement unless its source is recorded.
captionRules.placement: Use one shared caption lane outside both comparison panels.

fallbacks.action: Use a neutral process diagram based on the verified primary problem.

qaRules: Any quantitative comparison has a provenance source
The after state shows a real product capability
